To the south, the Ninth Ward is bounded by the Mississippi River. On the western or "upriver" side, the Ninth Ward is bounded by (going from the Mississippi River north to Lake Pontchartrain) Franklin Avenue, then Almonaster Avenue, then People's Avenue. From the north end of People's Avenue, the boundary continues on a straight line north to Lake Pontchartrain: this line is the boundary between the Ninth and Eighth Wards. Lake Pontchartrain forms the north and northeastern ends of the ward. For much of the 18th century, the land just outside New Orleans' city limits -- that is, the land outside the area we call the French Quarter -- was occupied by the Morand Plantation and brickyard, much of which was later acquired by hat maker and real estate developer Claude Treme. Shortly after Treme acquired it, the Spanish government in 1794 dug the Claiborne Canal from the fledgling city to Bayou St. John, splitting the tract and, by making it more accessible, opening it up for development. According to the Data Center, Treme had sold off most of his land by 1810, and by 1812 it had been subdivided for development of the neighborhood that today bears his name.

neighborhood_overview:
The Lower Garden District is often confused with its more famous neighbor, the Upper Garden District, but it has a unique, eclectic flavor all its own. Centered around Coliseum Square, the area is one of graceful vistas and curving streets, replete with classical names like Dryades, Melpomene, and Terpsichore. Indeed, Lee Circle, originally named Tivoli Circle, was envisioned as an anchor for the nine streets that extend from it, all named after the nine muses. The houses here actually predate those of the Garden District proper, since they were built in the early years of the 19th century during the city's upriver expansion from the French Quarter. Since the area is still in the process of being revitalized, many magnificent homes can be purchased here at reasonable prices, especially for those willing to invest a little "sweat equity."

Tremé (/trəˈmeɪ/ trə-MAY) is a neighborhood in New Orleans, Louisiana that is adjacent to the French Quarter Neighborhood. It is sometimes called by its more formal French name, Faubourg Tremé.

Founded in the 1810s, it is one of the oldest neighborhoods in the city, and was initially the main neighborhood of its free people of color. Historically a racially mixed neighborhood, it remains an important center of the city's African-American and Créole culture, especially the modern brass band tradition. Some sources go so far as to call it the oldest Black neighborhood in the nation.

I am a small business owner in the mid city area New Orleans. I absolutely love this city the food the music the festivals and I do it all. 

Myself I’m a big FOODIE.  I have my favorites from neighborhood joints down the street to the White tablecloth Michelin star/James Beard award winning restaurants. Great thing about New Orleans you can find really YUM food just about anywhere. Many neighborhood joints have James Beard award winning chefs.  I am always discovering a new fave. 

Music I love live entertainment and we have GREAT Music venues throughout the city from the outdoor concerts, to the local dives or the seated performances at The Auditorium in Armstrong Park. 

Who doesn’t love a great Bar scene. New Orleans has many Bars in many neighborhoods. Starting with Bourbon St in The French Quarters, how about a hole in the wall in the Historic Treme’ or a  pool bar in the Bywater, Frenchmen St in the Marigny neighborhood and Magazine St in the Irish Channel. The list goes on and on and on. Lol 
 
We also have many great museums throughout the city everything’s on exhibit from our Culture to the history of the City. We have one of the best children’s museums completely hands on this is always a wonderful afternoon with the kids. New Orleans Museum of Art in City Park is one of my favorite because after touring the museum it’s a short walk through the park for Cafe’ o latte and Beignets at Café Du Monde’ City park location With indoor and outdoor dining. City Park is filled with many live oak trees. 

My goal is to help my Guest make the most of their stay here in The Big Easy.  I want to give a combination of things to see and do that takes you from the Art scene to the Zydeco music  scene.  I want to help you discover more than just the French Quarters I want you to have a real sense of what this city and our people are about by the time you leave. :-) 

Laissez les bons temps rouler
“Let the good times roll”

name: Luxe, Sunlit Home | Heated Pool
description: This contemporary condo right outside of the Central Business District can fit up to 12 guests with its 5 bedrooms and 3 bathrooms. With its modern amenities, including a shared outdoor area, this home is perfect for those wanting to be in the middle of New Orleans. The professionally designed spaces offer open-concept layouts and kitchen & dining spaces perfect for entertaining.
neighborhood_overview:
Our home is located in the beautiful and historic Central City. We love this neighborhood and we think that you will too. Our home is minutes away from the historic streetcars that will take you to the heart of the French Quarter or into the Historic Garden District. At your doorstep are Greek revival and Victorian mansions, museums, and world-class restaurants. Walk down Magazine Street and explore the miles of galleries, antique stores, and boutiques waiting for you there. Or simply walk the other direction a few minutes and tour around the CBD where some of New Orleans' best restaurants await.

All guests after booking will receive a list of recommendations including locals favorite spots, restaurants, and activities. We will provide detailed information and guides on the surrounding area to enhance your overall experience.

Best known for the great live music district on Frenchmen Street, the Marigny also offers neighborhood cafes & businesses, historic architecture, and more. It has the air of what the French Quarter was in it's golden days. It has a few small hotels, and many bed-and-breakfasts, as well as a number of good restaurants, coffee shops, and music venues. Its "heart" is Washington Square Park (bounded by Frenchmen Street, Royal Street, Dauphine Street, and Elysian Fields Avenue). This historic neighborhood, with its labyrinthine cobblestone streets and ornate ironwork balconies, is a captivating blend of the city's storied past and its vibrant present. As you wander through the Quarter's narrow alleys and bustling squares, you'll find yourself transported to a place where centuries of culture converge in a symphony of colors, sounds, and flavors.

The architecture of the French Quarter tells a tale of resilience and adaptation, with its European influences evident in the Spanish courtyards, Creole townhouses, and French-inspired facades. neighborhood_overview:
Nestled along the banks of the Mississippi River, the French Quarter stands as an enduring testament to the soul and spirit of New Orleans. This historic neighborhood, with its labyrinthine cobblestone streets and ornate ironwork balconies, is a captivating blend of the city's storied past and its vibrant present. As you wander through the Quarter's narrow alleys and bustling squares, you'll find yourself transported to a place where centuries of culture converge in a symphony of colors, sounds, and flavors.

The architecture of the French Quarter tells a tale of resilience and adaptation, with its European influences evident in the Spanish courtyards, Creole townhouses, and French-inspired facades. Amidst these architectural treasures, you'll encounter an eclectic mix of art galleries, antique shops, and boutiques, each offering a glimpse into the local artistry and craftsmanship that make the Quarter a true haven for art enthusiasts and collectors.

neighborhood_overview:
Nestled at the crossroads of culture, history, and resilience lies the vibrant Treme neighborhood in New Orleans. As one of the city's most iconic and oldest neighborhoods, Treme boasts a rich tapestry of traditions, music, art, and stories that have shaped its identity over centuries. From the moment you step onto its storied streets, you're transported to a place where the past and present coexist harmoniously, each brick and note telling a tale of its storied history.

Treme's origins trace back to the 18th century, making it one of the oldest African American neighborhoods in the United States. Its name is derived from Claude Treme, a Frenchman who once owned the land upon which the neighborhood was built. Throughout its history, Treme has been a crucible of diverse cultures and backgrounds, blending African, French, Spanish, Creole, and Native American influences into a captivating melange that defines its character.

description:

neighborhood_overview: Everyone agrees. Uptown’s got the looks in the family, bless its heart. Those handsome neighborhoods, like the St. Charles Avenue streetcar, trundle upriver, unfolding as a series of distinctive names: Oretha Castle Haley, The Garden District, Irish Channel, Riverside, the Black Pearl, Carrollton. Uptown’s homes -- gleaming white and tiered like wedding cakes or shot-gunned into long, narrow lots – are the place’s glory and sheltered by canopies of leafy green or family trees as branched and blossoming as any ancient magnolia. The air’s opulent with the scent of jasmine and a slower, grander age. Uptown, where white tablecloths still cover two-tops. The waiter knows both your name and your preferences. A gin fizz? The crabmeat salad? Satsuma orange ice cream? They’re all on offer, as are the dazzling array of goods. The smart shops on Oak and Maple, Freret and Magazine, rival anything anywhere else. But this is Uptown, sugar. Once you’re here, there’s no reason – not ever – to leave.<b

North of the noise and saturated color of the Quarter is a New Orleans neighborhood that’s perfected the art of living. “Welcome to Mid-City,” read the signs on the neutral ground. And that’s truth in advertising. It’s the kind of place where your auto mechanic invites you to a crawfish boil and a total stranger may buy you a drink at an Irish pub or a cannoli at an Italian bakery. Take the red streetcar line up Canal to the Cemeteries (Mid-City’s dead neighbors are as interesting as the live ones) or bike the new 2.6-mile-long Lafitte Greenway that stretches from Basin Street to Carrollton Avenue and, conveniently, past a po’ boy shop or two – or 17 – with a sno-ball shop and a micro-brewery thrown in for good measure. neighborhood_overview:
North of the noise and saturated color of the Quarter is a New Orleans neighborhood that’s perfected the art of living. “Welcome to Mid-City,” read the signs on the neutral ground. It’s the kind of place where your auto mechanic invites you to a crawfish boil and a total stranger may buy you a drink at an Irish pub or a cannoli at an Italian bakery. Take the red streetcar line up Canal to the Cemeteries (Mid-City’s dead neighbors are as interesting as the live ones) or bike the new 2.6-mile-long Lafitte Greenway that stretches from Basin Street to Carrollton Avenue and, conveniently, past a po’ boy shop or two – or 17 – with a sno-ball shop and a micro-brewery thrown in for good measure. Buttermilk biscuits. Live music. A bowl of Vietnamese pho. Who wouldn’t want to visit? Eat. Drink. Get up here.

neighborhood_overview:
If you’re on the hunt for a home with a front porch, then Mid City New Orleans should definitely be on your short list. neighborhood_overview: The Faubourg Marigny, commonly just Marigny, is a hip neighborhood just "below" (down river from) the French Quarter. Best known for the great live music district on Frenchmen Street, the Marigny also offers neighborhood cafes & businesses, historic architecture, and more. It has the air of what the French Quarter was in it's golden days. It has a few small hotels, and many bed-and-breakfasts, as well as a number of good restaurants, coffee shops, and music venues. Architecturally, the Marigny is known for its many styles of Creole cottages, most of which date to the 19th century. Its "heart" is Washington Square Park (bounded by Frenchmen Street, Royal Street, Dauphine Street, and Elysian Fields Avenue). Frenchmen Street is the main nightlife district, with half a dozen live music clubs and just as many restaurants in four short blocks. Located on the northern border of the French Quarter above Rampart Street, Tremé is a uniquely historic neighborhood--one of the oldest neighborhoods in New Orleans. Early in the city's history, it was the main neighborhood of free people of color, and remains an important center of the city's Creole culture, especially the modern brass band tradition.
The modern Tremé neighborhood began as the Morand Plantation and two forts—St. Ferdinand and St. John. Near the end of the 18th century, Claude Tremé purchased the land from the original plantation owner. Within a few decades, the Carondelet Canal was built from the French Quarter to Bayou St. John, splitting the land. Developers began building subdivisions throughout the area to house a diverse population.

name: The NOLA Nest
description: This home is newly renovated with a peaceful, clean, minimalistic vibe. You are minutes from the French quarters and about 20 minutes from many hospitals in the area. This is an ideal home for travel nurses. We’ve put a bonfire set up on your private deck to really make use of the space. Being outdoors to relax is just as important to us as being inside.
neighborhood_overview:
Many tourist spots include The French quarters, Magazine street in Uptown, City Park in Midtown, and many options for Plantation and swamp tours. The closest plantation is Destrehan which is 28 minutes away. There are outstanding choices for Cajun cuisine and seafood throughout town. Take full advantage of it. You won’t be disappointed.

For any travel nurses this is a great location to commute to work from. I am a nurse and worked in the city with a quick 10 min drive. Also nice to come back home to a quiet, clean spot after a long day.

The neighbors are friendly and kind, which we are so grateful for. Everything is only a drive away. For anyone that has not been to New Orleans before, it does have a high crime rate and it is our responsibility to be transparent about that. Always keep your doors locked and check your surroundings no matter where you are in this beautiful historic city.

The first plantation owner to do this, Bernard Marigny de Mandeville, owned the land just downriver from Esplanade Avenue.

name: Central Business District Monthly Rental - 1BR/1BA
description: Spacious condo with natural lighting and beautiful wood floors in the Warehouse District located directly on Julia Street. Offers quick access to the many bars, shops, galleries and restaurants. From James Beard Award-winning restaurants to chic bistros and low key sandwich shops, the neighborhood is filled with amazing dining options. Steps away from museums & art galleries, the Warehouse District is a culture-seeker’s playground.
neighborhood_overview: In the Warehouse Arts District it’s 19th century paving stones and 21st Century rooftop swimming pools, grilled Gulf redfish and warm baguettes, a B-17 Flying Fortress called “My Gal Sal” and an African-American self-taught artist named Clementine Hunter. This urbane neighborhood is where New Orleans’ past and present meet up for drinks while the future texts “I’m on my way.” Famed for institutions like the National WWII Museum and the Ogden Museum of Southern Art and events like the First Saturday Julia Street art walk, it also offers smaller delights: Watching young ballerinas en pointe framed in a plate glass window; sharing a pizza beneath the stars or brunching on coconut French toast. Vital and alive, the Warehouse District glows like those old school Edison light bulbs. Delight in the art on its walls and celebrate the life in its streets.

name: Roami at Duncan Plaza | Studio
description: Welcome to Roami at Duncan Plaza, nestled in the heart of New Orleans' vibrant Central Business District. Immerse yourself in the city's rich culture, tantalizing cuisine, and lively music scene, all just steps away from your doorstep. Whether you're here for business or pleasure, your stylish and comfortable space provides a memorable stay in the Big Easy.
neighborhood_overview:
Step outside and discover the bustling streets of the Central Business District, where a world of excitement awaits. Indulge in mouthwatering Creole and Cajun cuisine at nearby restaurants, or sample freshly shucked oysters at a local seafood joint. Immerse yourself in the soulful sounds of jazz music drifting from historic clubs and lively street performers. For a dose of history, stroll to nearby landmarks like Lafayette Square and the historic French Quarter, where you can admire stunning architecture and soak up the city's unique charm. Need a break from the urban hustle? Head to the nearby beaches along the Gulf Coast for sun, sand, and relaxation.

Nearby Attractions

Audubon Aquarium of the Americas (1.2 miles): Expansive aquatic exhibit showcase.

Bourbon Street and Canal Street (0.5 miles): Iconic nightlife and shopping hub.

House of Blues (1.0 miles): Vibrant music venue and restaurant.

Port of New Orleans (2.2 miles): Major
host_about:
Our spaces are purposefully designed to inspire connection and create a transformative vacation, where guests create memories that will stay with them long after they leave.

Founded in 2016, Roami was born from the belief that travelers should not be forced to choose between two flawed options: cramped and expensive hotel rooms or inconsistent and unpredictable vacation rentals. 

Roami provides a memorable stay without compromise.

name: Hideaway w/ Hot Tub, Downtown Views, 2 Balconies!
description:
Take it easy at this unique and tranquil getaway.

Algiers Point is New Orleans’ best kept secret. You’ll enjoy watching the boats go by on the balcony with a view of the GNO Bridge and skyline. This home is 10 blocks to the Ferry Terminal. You can walk along the levee, hop on the ferry, and it drops you off right on Canal Street in the FQ. There are several restaurants in walking distance.

This home has 2 large balconies, a hot tub, and beautiful, unobstructed views of the heart of the city.
neighborhood_overview:
A quiet suburb on the Mississippi River’s West Bank, Algiers Point is a mix of homey pubs, small art galleries and quaint Creole cottages. Visitors cross via the New Orleans Ferry or the Crescent City Connection Bridge for views over to Jackson Square and the French Quarter. Joggers and cyclists follow the levee path, where open-air concerts at the Algiers Ferry Landing draw crowds

Things to not: Algiers is a true New Orleans neighborhood, and we encourage guests to research the neighborhood and surrounding area prior to booking

name: Roami at Canal Quarters | 2 Bed Combo | 2 Units
description: Welcome to Roami at Canal Quarters, where historical charm meets modern luxury in the heart of New Orleans. Nestled on the edge of the legendary French Quarter, we offers an authentic experience with contemporary comforts. Situated on Canal Street, this prime location invites you to immerse yourself in the rich music, cuisine, and culture of one of the world’s most iconic neighborhoods.
neighborhood_overview:
Step into the rhythm of New Orleans at the edge of the French Quarter, where historic charm meets modern energy. Surrounded by iconic jazz clubs, vibrant art galleries, and world-famous cuisine, this neighborhood invites you to explore every corner. Just outside your door, Canal Street pulses with life, offering a direct line into the heart of the city’s most storied district. Whether you're here to dance through the night on Bourbon Street, savor bold Creole flavors, or take in the beauty of French Quarter architecture, everything is just moments away. For even more adventure, hop on the Canal Street streetcar and discover the Garden District, the riverfront, and beyond.

Nearby Attractions

Audubon Aquarium of the Americas (0.7 miles): Expansive aquatic exhibit showcase.

Bourbon Street and Canal Street (Steps away—you’re on it!): Iconic nightlife and shopping hub.

House of Blues (0.4 miles): Vibrant music venue and restaurant.

Our spaces are purposefully designed to inspire connection and create a transformative vacation, where guests create memories that will stay with them long after they leave.

Founded in 2016, Roami was born from the belief that travelers should not be forced to choose between two flawed options: cramped and expensive hotel rooms or inconsistent and unpredictable vacation rentals. 

Roami provides a memorable stay without compromise.

Let the soul of New Orleans surround you in a neighborhood where every block pulses with culture, color, and sound. Just steps from your door, the French Quarter invites you to wander its historic streets, where Creole townhouses, hidden courtyards, and centuries-old landmarks tell the story of the city’s vibrant past. House of Blues (0.4 miles): Intimate venue featuring live music and classic Southern cuisine.

Roami provides a memorable stay without compromise.

neighborhood_overview:
Oretha Castle Haley Boulevard is a historic and culturally rich corridor in Central City, New Orleans. Once a thriving commercial district in the early 20th century, it has experienced a remarkable revival, transforming into a vibrant hub for arts, dining, and community-driven initiatives. Named after the prominent civil rights activist Oretha Castle Haley, the boulevard is a symbol of resilience and cultural significance.

The area is also well-connected to other parts of the city, sitting just a short drive or streetcar ride from the French Quarter, the Garden District, and the Central Business District. This makes it an attractive location for residents who want easy access to the city's top attractions while enjoying a neighborhood with a strong sense of identity and history.

description:
Welcome to your Bywater loft retreat!

- Stylish 2BR escape blending cozy comfort with bold New Orleans character.
- Relax in the bright living area with unique décor, fast Wi-Fi, flat-screen TV, and a dedicated workspace.

neighborhood_overview:
Known for its colorful street murals, the Bywater neighborhood has a bohemian vibe, with plenty of outdoor cafes, boisterous dive bars and hip restaurants. Quirky boutiques selling handmade goods dot the area, while buzzy St. Roch Market offers southern gourmet specialties in a stylishly updated Victorian food hall. Trails, picnic spots and sweeping city views are the draw at riverside Crescent Park.

A vibrant art scene - with local artisans' galleries, funky live music venues, and art markets, embodies the essence of these adjacent neighborhoods. The food scene here is mixed with trendy spots and locally founded, casual digs - take your pick. Explore the St. Claude Arts District, Crescent Park on the riverfront, and more.

Immerse yourself in the city's rich culture, tantalizing cuisine, and lively music scene, all just steps away from your doorstep. neighborhood_overview:
Step outside and discover the bustling streets of the Central Business District, where a world of excitement awaits. Indulge in mouthwatering Creole and Cajun cuisine at nearby restaurants, or sample freshly shucked oysters at a local seafood joint. For a dose of history, stroll to nearby landmarks like Lafayette Square and the historic French Quarter, where you can admire stunning architecture and soak up the city's unique charm. Need a break from the urban hustle? Head to the nearby beaches along the Gulf Coast for sun, sand, and relaxation.

Roami provides a memorable stay without compromise.

description: Experience classic New Orleans charm at The Lafayette by Kasa, a 1916 historic landmark along the St. Charles Streetcar line next to Lafayette Square, and just a short walk to the French Quarter and the stunning antebellum mansions of the Garden District. neighborhood_overview:
The Lafayette offers an unbeatable location nestled between two of New Orleans' most iconic neighborhoods—the lively French Quarter and the enchanting Garden District. With its central position, you're just steps away from the heart of the city's eclectic cultural scene. Stroll through the vibrant French Quarter, where jazz fills the air, and renowned restaurants and local boutiques line the historic streets. For a more serene experience, explore the Garden District's oak-shaded avenues, where grand antebellum mansions and lush gardens provide a stunning display of classic New Orleans architecture. Discover the rich history, charm, and unique character that make New Orleans a favorite destination for travelers worldwide, with The Lafayette as your perfect home base.

- Mother’s Restaurant, 0.3 miles away
- Peche Seafood

host_about:
I love traveling the world, particularly Latin America.  I have an affection for things leather-bound, rustic, old, or filled with character.  I am always happy to pass up on modern conveniences.  Triathlon enthusiast.

Favorite places to visit in the United States:  Provincetown, Massachusetts;  Asheville, North Carolina;  New Orleans, Louisiana;  Big Sur, California.  Favorite places to visit in the world:  Mexico, Argentina, Ecuador, Italy, Tunisia, and Vietnam.

Favorite wines:  Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Valpolicella Ripasso, Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.

My favorite poem - "If" by Rudyard Kipling:
If you can keep your head when all about you   
    Are losing theirs and blaming it on you,   
If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you,
    But make allowance for their doubting too;   
If you can wait and not be tired by waiting,
    Or being lied about, don’t deal in lies,
Or being hated, don’t give way to hating,
    And yet don’t look too good, nor talk too wise:

If you can dream—and not make dreams your master;   
    If you can think—and not make thoughts your aim;   
If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster
    And treat those two impostors just the same;   
If you can bear to hear the truth you’ve spoken
    Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools,
Or watch the things you gave your life to, broken,
    And stoop and build ’em up with worn-out tools:

If you can make one heap of all your winnings
    And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss,
And lose, and start again at your beginnings
    And never breathe a word about your loss;
If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew
    To serve your turn long after they are gone,   
And so hold on when there is nothing in you
    Except the Will which says to them: ‘Hold on!’

If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue,   
    Or walk with Kings—nor lose the common touch,
If neither foes nor loving friends can hurt you,
    If all men count with you, but none too much;
If you can fill the unforgiving minute
    With sixty seconds’ worth of distance run,   
Yours is the Earth and everything that’s in it,   
    And—which is more—you’ll be a Man, my son!

neighborhood_overview:
Steps to the LaFitte Greenway!

North of the noise and saturated color of the Quarter is a New Orleans neighborhood that’s perfected the art of living. “Welcome to Mid-City,” read the signs on the neutral ground. And that’s truth in advertising. It’s the kind of place where your auto mechanic invites you to a crawfish boil and a total stranger may buy you a drink at an Irish pub or a cannoli at an Italian bakery. Take the red streetcar line up Canal to the Cemeteries (Mid-City’s dead neighbors are as interesting as the live ones) or bike the new 2.6-mile-long Lafitte Greenway that stretches from Basin Street to Carrollton Avenue and, conveniently, past a po’ boy shop or two – or 17 – with a sno-ball shop and a micro-brewery thrown in for good measure. Buttermilk biscuits. Live music. A bowl of Vietnamese pho. Who wouldn’t want to visit? Eat. Drink. Get up here.
If you have any questions about the neighborhood, please send us a message!

Located between the Garden District and Riverside, this home features a blend of historic charm and modern flair. The area is known for its wonderful atmosphere, featuring an array of locally-owned boutiques, trendy cafes, and diverse restaurants. Magazine Street is lined with beautifully preserved 19th-century architecture, including Victorian homes and Creole cottages, all under a canopy of lush oak trees, making it one of the most walkable areas in the city.

Cultural attractions like Audubon Park and Zoo are nearby, offering green spaces and recreational activities. Tulane and Loyola universities are within a few miles of the home as well. Frequent neighborhood events, markets, and festivals celebrate the unique New Orleans heritage, fostering a strong sense of community. The neighborhood's charm, vitality, and excellent connectivity make it a desirable place to live and visit.

There are several grocery stores within a mile of the home, including a Fresh Market

This neighborhood is right next to the French Quarter, and close to everything fun.

Located on the northern border of the French Quarter above Rampart Street, Tremé is a uniquely historic neighborhood--one of the oldest neighborhoods in New Orleans. Early in the city's history, it was the main neighborhood of free people of color, and remains an important center of the city's Creole culture, especially the modern brass band tradition.
The modern Tremé neighborhood began as the Morand Plantation and two forts—St. Ferdinand and St. John. Near the end of the 18th century, Claude Tremé purchased the land from the original plantation owner. Within a few decades, the Carondelet Canal was built from the French Quarter to Bayou St. John, splitting the land. Developers began building subdivisions throughout the area to house a diverse population.

neighborhood_overview:
Our home is located in the heart of the New Orleans Uptown/ Carrollton -- a classic New Orleans neighborhood with a combination of old homes, all kinds of local businesses and corner restaurants and bars. There's a little bit of commerce and a whole lot of character!
Uptown Carrollton is a historic neighborhood in New Orleans, Louisiana, that's part of the larger Uptown section of the city. It's known for its grand mansions, leafy streets, and historic buildings. 
* Carrollton was originally a separate town that was laid out in 1833. 
* It was annexed by New Orleans in 1874. 
* The area was once a slave plantation owned by a Frenchman. 
The neighborhood and Avenue are pronounced "kaa-rull-ton" or "kaa-ril-tin" by residents and other uptowners, but many people from the downtown parts of New Orleans (especially those born in the mid-20th century and earlier) pronounce the names as "Karl-ton".

neighborhood_overview: North of the noise and saturated color of the Quarter is a New Orleans neighborhood that’s perfected the art of living. “Welcome to Mid-City,” read the signs on the neutral ground. And that’s truth in advertising. It’s the kind of place where your auto mechanic invites you to a crawfish boil and a total stranger may buy you a drink at an Irish pub or a cannoli at an Italian bakery. Take the red streetcar line up Canal to the Cemeteries (Mid-City’s dead neighbors are as interesting as the live ones) or bike the new 2.6-mile-long Lafitte Greenway that stretches from Basin Street to Carrollton Avenue and, conveniently, past a po’ boy shop or two – or 17 – with a sno-ball shop and a micro-brewery thrown in for good measure. Buttermilk biscuits. Live music. A bowl of Vietnamese pho. Who wouldn’t want to visit? Eat. Drink. Get up here.

name: Peaceful Bywater Home | Heated Pool | Quiet Stay
description: This upscale home in the quiet residential Bywater neighborhood can fit up to 10 guests with its 5 bedrooms and 5 bathrooms. With its modern amenities, including a heated pool, this home is perfect for those looking for a relaxing and peaceful stay in the middle of New Orleans. The professionally designed spaces offer open-concept layouts and kitchen & dining spaces perfect for entertaining.
neighborhood_overview: The Bywater is a peaceful, friendly, and laid-back neighborhood, offering a perfect balance of charm and convenience. Rated as one of the top 10 hippest neighborhoods in the country by The New Yorker, it provides a relaxed retreat while keeping you close to the city's vibrant culture. We are just steps from Crescent Park and a short Uber/Lyft ride to the French Quarter. Right across the street, you'll find a top-rated local coffee shop, and within walking distance, some of the best bars and restaurants in New Orleans—including our personal favorite, Bacchanal. Whether you're here to unwind with family, collaborate with colleagues, or explore with friends, the Bywater offers something for everyone in a quiet and welcoming setting.
